attempted_claim: Let PVI_theta be the sixth Painleve equation at resonant fixed exponents theta=(3/2,1/2,0,1/2) with integer differences, reduced by an explicit W(D4^(1)) Schlesinger word to minimal length with Sakai D4^(1) nodal -2-curve ledger, and fix the explicit unipotent monodromy triple (M0 unipotent Jordan block, Mt,M1 semisimple of stated traces). Decide: either (A) there exists a logarithmic transcendent at t=0 with this triple and leading logarithmic coefficient c<>0 explicitly, exhibited by closed-form Jimbo-type asymptotics plus verified analytic-continuation branching, or (B) every solution with this triple is meromorphic or Riccati at t=0 with c=0, proved by an explicit resonance-residue computation plus the nodal ledger ruling out the logarithmic branch. A complete answer proves one alternative with the triple, the coefficient c or its vanishing, and the ledger certificate explicit, new relative to the Saito-Terajima Riccati, Mazzocco rational, and Lisovyy-Tykhyy finite-orbit tables.
claim_type: logarithmic versus meromorphic dichotomy at resonance
decisive_failure: The target data as stated are contradictory: theta0=3/2 forces a diagonalizable M0 of trace 0, so the prescribed unipotent triple does not exist and neither target branch has a well-posed subject. No corrected-parameter program could be completed to Audit standard in the remaining time.
